b: A non-shoppable video is a video that shows, reviews or recommends a product but carries no built-in route to buy it: no product link, no anchor, no cart button. The term exists because commerce platforms now treat the purchase path as a property a video either has or lacks. On TikTok Shop, where the phrase is used most precisely, a video becomes shoppable when a seller or affiliate creator attaches a product link to it. Every other video, including a creator's enthusiastic but unlinked review, falls into the non-shoppable bucket. That bucket is large, and as of November 2026 platforms have started building tools to sell from it.
A label defined by what is missing
The word is a retronym. Until platforms began attaching purchase paths to video, no video was shoppable and the default state needed no name.
Three conditions usually decide which side of the line a video falls on:
A product link or anchor. On TikTok Shop, a product link (also called an anchor link) appears as a tappable tag that opens a product page inside the app.
A transaction path inside the platform. A spoken discount code or an on-screen URL generally does not count, because the platform cannot attribute the sale.
Eligibility of the account and product. A creator outside the affiliate program, an unlisted product or a restricted account cannot add a link.

The same split exists in paid video. A standard 30-second spot on connected TV (CTV, meaning television content streamed over the internet to a TV set) is non-shoppable. The same spot with a remote-control "add to cart" overlay is a shoppable ad, the category covered in the PPC Land explainer on shoppable ads.
How a video becomes shoppable, and why most do not

On TikTok Shop, the mechanics are set at posting. A seller posting from its own account, or a creator enrolled in the affiliate program, selects a product from a showcase and attaches it before publishing. If an order follows through that link, the creator earns a commission, which TikTok calls cost per sale (CPS). The product tagging step is what turns an ordinary clip into a sales channel and what lets TikTok count gross merchandise value, or GMV, against it.

A video can end up without a link for several reasons. Many creators post product content without joining the affiliate program, some brands run unlinked awareness content, and customers post unboxings and reviews, a form of user-generated content no seller controls. And since 2026, TikTok has also capped how many linked videos an account may post.

Since May 11, 2026, TikTok Shop has limited each US account to 25 shoppable videos a day, and PPC Land reported that the daily limits were introduced to promote content quality across all US merchants and creators. A separate rule targets low-effort posts. Under TikTok's Creator Enforcement Policy, a creator who posts five or more "non-interactive" TikTok Shop videos within seven days can be restricted for seven days, during which only seven videos may carry product links. Videos beyond that number are published without links. Enforcement itself manufactures non-shoppable video: the content stays up, the purchase path goes.

Sources disagree on when that rule began. PPC Land dated the interaction-based limit to January 19, 2026. BigSeller, a third-party seller-software company, wrote on March 5, 2026 that "Beginning March 30, TikTok will track your content quality over a rolling 7-day period," citing TikTok's Malaysian seller university rather than the US one. The two dates may reflect different markets, but neither source reconciles them.

The newest mechanism aims squarely at this category. TikTok's US Seller University guide "Post-view Search," updated on November 27, 2026, lets sellers attach search suggestions and products to videos that feature their goods, including videos posted by creators. PPC Land covered the feature today.
The workflow runs in five steps for a seller's own videos:
Open Search Optimization in Seller Center and choose a video from the My videos, Creator videos or Top videos tab.
Add up to five search keywords. TikTok suggests queries of two to six English words naming brands, product types, features, styles or use cases.
For the seller's own videos only, write a comment of up to 500 characters, posted from the linked TikTok account, which can be pinned.
Link up to 20 products, searchable by name or ID.
Preview and save. Changes take effect the next day, which TikTok writes as T+1.

Creator videos follow the same path without the comment step, because, according to the guide, "a seller cannot speak on behalf of a creator." Sellers can edit up to 20 videos in one batch and receive up to 10 recommended videos at a time. For videos by accounts with no relationship to the seller, TikTok says its system identifies matching products and routes eligible videos to the seller's backend, adding that "current same-product recognition accuracy is 91%." The guide does not explain how that figure was measured.

The key design choice is the default filter. According to the guide, the system shows non-shoppable videos, "videos without a product link or cart," first. TikTok's reasoning is that shoppable videos already give viewers a route to the product page, while unlinked videos build interest without a direct path to purchase. The guide also states that sellers are not charged any extra affiliate commission for optimizing non-shoppable videos.

Paid media offers a parallel route. According to TikTok's Ads Help Center, a campaign with the Sales objective can add product links to an in-feed video ad, overriding whatever the organic post carried. A non-shoppable organic video becomes shoppable as soon as money is spent behind it.
Why the distinction matters to marketers

The label decides what can be measured. A shoppable video produces orders and GMV that are attributed directly. A non-shoppable video produces views and searches, and any sale it causes appears elsewhere, often credited to search or another video. TikTok's own dashboard for the new feature reports video impressions, search volume, search product impressions, search orders and search GMV, an attempt to close part of that gap.

Shoppable video and live shopping together account for 60% to 70% of top sellers' revenue in Germany, according to TikTok data cited in PPC Land's coverage of TikTok's shoppable video content guide. Linked posts are rationed at 25 a day per account; unlinked product content has no comparable cap, so every new limit enlarges the non-shoppable pool.

On CTV, most inventory remains non-shoppable and buyers want purchase paths. An IAB study cited in the PPC Land shoppable ads explainer found in July 2026 that 39% of buyers named the lack of click-through as the main obstacle to CTV. Formats such as Amazon's add-to-cart overlays on Samsung TV Plus convert standard spots.

The commission question is the most contested. If a seller attaches products and search terms to a creator's unlinked review, and an order follows, the guide states that no additional CPS commission is charged. It does not say whether the creator receives anything. Creators who chose not to link, or were blocked by a cap, may see their content monetized without payment. TikTok's guide does not address creator consent beyond withholding the comment feature.

Measurement is the second issue. TikTok has not published an attribution window for search orders that follow a suggested keyword. The UNICE case study in the guide, covering 160 videos between October 28 and November 2, 2026, reported keywords showing on 117 of them (73.1%), 23,060 keyword impressions and "observed growth" of 30% or more in search orders and GMV. TikTok's own footnote calls these "observed-period results only; not a causal lift claim or performance guarantee." The 91% product-recognition figure carries no stated method.
Third, the label is unstable. A video can be shoppable at posting, lose its link through enforcement, and regain a purchase path through Post-view Search or a paid ad.
Finally, neither the IAB nor the Media Rating Council (MRC) defines the term, so each platform draws its own line.

Non-skippable video. A non-skippable ad is one the viewer cannot skip, such as Google's non-skippable in-stream format. Skippability concerns viewing; shoppability concerns purchase. A non-skippable ad can be shoppable or not.

Non-interactive video. TikTok uses "non-interactive" in enforcement for low-effort shop content, such as still images over music. A non-interactive video may carry a product link until a restriction removes it, at which point it becomes non-shoppable too.

Interactive ads. An interactive CTV ad can let viewers request information or watch a trailer without offering a purchase. As the shoppable ads explainer puts it, every shoppable ad is interactive, but not the reverse.
Organic video. Organic means unpaid. Organic posts on TikTok Shop are often shoppable, and paid ads can be non-shoppable, so the two distinctions cut across each other.

The category moved from passive description to operational target in 2026. TikTok's January and May rules limited how many videos could carry links. The Post-view Search guide, updated on November 27, 2026 and reported by PPC Land today, makes unlinked videos the default focus of a seller tool, available to US sellers only. On the television side, the expansion of shoppable formats through deals such as LG Ad Solutions' agreement with KERV is shrinking the share of streaming inventory that remains non-shoppable. In both, platforms are attaching purchase paths after the fact, rather than leaving that to whoever made the video.

Who: Sellers, affiliate creators and ordinary users who post product videos, and the platforms that decide whether those videos carry a purchase path, most explicitly TikTok Shop. On the paid side, advertisers and CTV publishers deciding whether to add shoppable overlays.
What: A video that features or recommends a product but has no product link, anchor or cart, so the viewer cannot buy from inside it. The term exists as the counterpart to shoppable video.

When: The distinction became necessary once buy buttons appeared on social content in 2014 and TikTok Shop launched in the US on September 12, 2023. It became an operational category in 2026, with TikTok's posting limits from May 11 and its Post-view Search guide updated on November 27, 2026.
Where: Social commerce apps, above all TikTok Shop in the US, as well as streaming TV and other video advertising where standard spots lack a purchase path.

Why: It separates content whose sales can be attributed directly from content whose influence is harder to measure. Platforms now treat non-shoppable video as unrealized sales, which raises open questions about creator commissions, consent and how the resulting orders are counted.
